name: Expected Value
miniText: How can uncertain individual outcomes yield a predictable average value? NetLogo Expected Value assigns numerical values to patches according to chosen ratios, calculates a probability-weighted expectation, and lets a moving sampler collect values into repeated totals. Jaynes [1] supplies the weighted-expectation interpretation, Durrett [2] formalizes means and dependence, and Wilensky [3] provides relevant research on learning statistical regularities through simulation. The original Procedures use a local walk for the sampler; successive observations need not be independent draws from the whole patch population. Consequently, finite-run agreement depends on spatial arrangement and movement as well as assigned proportions. The simulation illustrates the distinction between an outcome's probability and its numerical worth. It does not make the expected value a guaranteed payoff, nor does a matching long-run mean alone establish unbiased or independent sampling.
